title: With Broken Heart and Contrite Sigh
description: With Broken Heart and Contrite Sigh in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Cornelius Elven wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 418.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: With bro-ken heart and con-trite sigh, A trem-bling sin-ner, Lord, I cry; Thy par-doning grace is rich and free; O God, be mer-ci-ful to me!

lines: With broken heart and contrite sigh,
A trembling sinner, Lord, I cry;
Thy pardoning grace is rich and free;
O God, be merciful to me!
I smite upon my troubled breast,
With deep and conscious guilt opprest;
Christ and His Cross my only plea;
O God, be merciful to me!
Far off I stand with tearful eyes
Nor dare uplift them to the skies;
But Thou dost all my anguish see;
O God, be merciful to me!
Nor alms nor deeds that I have done
Can for a single sin atone;
To Calvary alone I flee;
O God, be merciful to me!
And when, redeemed from sin and hell,
With all the ransomed throng I dwell,
My raptured song shall ever be,
God has been merciful to me!

licence: Public domain: Cornelius Elven died in 1873.
credits: Words by Cornelius Elven (1797–1873), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
